title: String to Number
story: A user types '42' into your app. But it's just text — you need an actual number. Parsing '42' works fine, but what about 'hello'? That's when you discover XIOM's built-in string-to-int converter.
why: `string.str_to_int()` is your first encounter with a built-in function returning Result — it's the bridge between user text input and numeric computation.
analogy: string.str_to_int is like a currency exchange booth — you hand over paper with numbers written on it (Str), and the cashier either gives you real coins (Ok(Int)) or rejects your fake bill (Err).
try_it: Try parsing these strings: "007", "+42", "3.5", "1_000". Which ones work? Can you write a function that strips whitespace before parsing? (Hint: you can't yet — but think about what you'd need.)
tips: `string.str_to_int()` returns `Result[Int, Str]` — always handle both Ok and Err
Only pure integer strings parse — no commas, dots, spaces, or special characters
Chain parsing with .unwrap_or(0) when you want to silently ignore bad input
common_mistakes: Assuming all numeric-looking strings parse — "3.14" and "1,000" will fail
Using the parsed number without checking the Result — the compiler forces you to handle it
Calling string.str_to_int on an already-integer value — the function takes Str, not Int
